text: All offerors must be registered and maintain an active status in the System for Award Management (SAM) with the appropriate NAICS code, and must possess a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Offerors must submit a complete and signed SF30 for any applicable amendments, a complete price schedule, and a detailed capabilities statement or project narrative demonstrating technical knowledge and experience in the products/services described in the specifications, including all required shop drawings and product data. If quoting an "or equal" item, detailed product specifications/literature must be provided to confirm comparability. Offerors must provide at least three prior experience references for similar projects in scope and size within the past five years, including project descriptions and contact information for verification. Submissions must be sent via email to colette_riegelmayer@ios.doi.gov. Offerors are urged to inspect the site to satisfy themselves regarding local conditions affecting cost. Payment requests must be submitted electronically through the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) system; if unable to comply, a written waiver request must be submitted to the Contracting Officer with the proposal. Invoices must be PDF format, include pricing breakdown, contract number, date of service, date of invoice, and vendor letterhead. All required documents must be submitted according to the checklist.

text: The following requirements must be met for submission and contract performance: 1. Registration and Entity Identification: Offerors must be registered and maintain an active status in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of quote/proposal submission, at the time of award, and throughout the entire contract performance period. This registration must include the appropriate NAICS code found in block 10 on page 1 of the solicitation and must be considered a small business for the size standard associated with that NAICS code. Additionally, companies must obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 2. Submission Process: Quotes/proposals must be submitted via email to colette_riegelmayer@ios.doi.gov. If applicable, signed amendments (SF30) must be reviewed, acknowledged, and included in the final package. 3. Technical and Experience Requirements: Offerors must provide detailed capabilities statements, project narratives, or technical questionnaires demonstrating knowledge of and experience with the products/services described in the specifications. This must include prior experience references (preferably a minimum of 3) for similar projects/services that confirm successful completion of similar tasks as outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW). 4. Product and Technical Documentation: Submissions must include all required shop drawings and product data. If quoting an "or equal" item, a detailed product specification document/literature must be submitted to confirm comparability. 5. Site Inspection: Offerors are urged and expected to be site-inspected to satisfy themselves regarding all general and local conditions that may affect the cost of contract performance. 6. Payment and Invoicing: The Contractor must register for and use the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) for all payment requests, which must be submitted electronically. Required invoice attachments to the IPP include a PDF copy of the vendor invoice showing a pricing breakdown, contract number, date(s) of service, date of invoice, and vendor's standard letterhead. If the Contractor is unable to comply with the use of IPP, a written waiver request must be submitted to the Contracting Officer along with the proposal/quotation. 7. Regulatory and Legal Compliance: Regulatory clauses (such as as 52.225-20, 52.225-25, 52.240-90, 52.252-2, 52.252-6, 52.203-17, 52.203-19, 52.204-13, 52.204-19, 52.209-10, 52.212-4, 52.219-6, 52.219-28, 52.222-3, 52.222-19, 52.222-41, 52.222-42, 52.222-50, 52.222-62, 52.222-90, 52.223-5, 52.225-1, 52.226-7, 52.226-8) must be adhered to. Note: Deviations/Amendments may apply as specified in the clauses. 8. Small Business Status: Small business status must be maintained throughout the entire award/contract performance.

Payment requests must be submitted electronically through the U.S. Department of the

documents are required to be submitted as an attachment to the IPP invoice:
